preconditions.description: The integer k is within the valid range [1, 18].
The initial string s has length exactly 2^k - 1, where k is the input integer.

preconditions.expression: all(c in {'0', '1', '?'} for c in s)
preconditions.description: Every character in the initial string s is either '0', '1', or '?'.
The number of queries q is within the valid range [1, 200000].

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= p <= (2 ** k) - 1 for p, c in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query position p is within the valid range [1, 2^k - 1].

preconditions.expression: all(c in {'0', '1', '?'} for p, c in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query character c is either '0', '1', or '?'.

postconditions.description: For each query, the output is a newline-separated list of integers, where each integer is the number of possible winners f(s) after applying the query to the current string s. The string s_after_query is the result of applying the query to s, and s_after_queries is the sequence of strings after each query.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= f(s) <= 2**k for s in s_after_queries)
postconditions.description: For each string s, f(s) is the number of possible winners, which is an integer between 1 and 2^k (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: all(team in {1, 2, ..., 2**k} for s in s_after_queries for team in possible_winners(s))
postconditions.description: For each string s, every possible winner is a team index between 1 and 2^k (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: all(any(team == winner(s, replacement) for team in possible_winners(s)) for s in s_after_queries for replacement in possible_replacements(s))
postconditions.description: For each string s, every possible winner is a team that can be the champion for at least one valid replacement of '?' characters in s. Here, possible_replacements(s) is the set of all possible replacements of '?' with '0' or '1', and winner(s, replacement) is the champion after applying the replacement.

postconditions.expression: all(len(possible_winners(s)) == f(s) for s in s_after_queries)
postconditions.description: For each string s, f(s) is exactly the count of distinct possible winners.
